LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
 <security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
Sourcing this PKGBUILD executes only its global/top-level scope, which consists entirely of plain variable assignments and array definitions (`_name`, `pkgbase`, `pkgname`, `pkgver`, `source`, `sha256sums`, etc.). There are no command substitutions, no `eval` calls, no external tool invocations, and no network operations at the top level. Running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` will therefore not download anything and will not execute any untrusted payload.

The `package_*()` functions contain `install` commands, but those functions are not invoked by `--printsrcinfo`, so they are out of scope for this narrow gate and will be reviewed in the full package audit. The `source` array points to the project's own Codeberg releases and all four checksums are pinned (none are `SKIP`). No genuinely malicious top-level behavior is present.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>
Safe: top-level scope contains only variable assignments; no code execution risk.
</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for .SRCINFO:
 <security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This is a standard AUR `.SRCINFO` file for a font package named `garamontio-font`. It contains no executable commands, no scripts, and no build or install instructions that could contain malicious logic. All sources are pinned to specific release artifacts (`.zip` and `.tar.gz`) downloaded over HTTPS from the project's own upstream repository on `codeberg.org` (the `m-casanova/Garamontio` project page). This is the expected supply chain, not an unrelated or unexpected host.

All four source files have explicit sha256 checksums (no `SKIP` entries), which helps verify the integrity of the download. The `provides` entries are ordinary font package metadata. Nothing in this file exfiltrates data, downloads or executes untrusted code, uses obfuscated strings, modifies system files, or attempts any privilege escalation. The file is consistent with standard Arch packaging and presents no security concerns.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>Standard font .SRCINFO; pinned upstream sources, no suspicious behavior.</summary>
</security_assessment>

[2/3] Reviewing PKGBUILD...
+ Reviewed .SRCINFO. Status: SAFE -- Standard font .SRCINFO; pinned upstream sources, no suspicious behavior.
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This is a standard font packaging PKGBUILD. All four sources are downloaded over HTTPS from the project's own upstream at codeberg.org/m-casanova/Garamontio, and each source has a hardcoded SHA-256 checksum -- no SKIP entries, no unverified downloads, no VCS or mutable-ref fetching. There is no `build()`, and the three `package_*()` functions only run `install` to copy `.otf`/`.ttf` font files and the OFL license into `$pkgdir/usr/share/fonts/...` and `$pkgdir/usr/share/licenses/...`, which is exactly the expected behavior for a font package. No `eval`, base64, obfuscated strings, network-exfiltrating commands, `curl|bash`, or execution of anything from the downloaded archives (the source tarball is checksum-verified but never unpacked or run). The maintainer line also matches a well-known Arch packager.

Minor non-security observations: the variable-font glob `${_name}*.ttf` uses a lowercase prefix while the other packages use `${_name^}-`, so if it fails to match the actual filenames the build would simply fail -- a packaging nit, not a threat. Also, one of the checksums shown in the transcript (the second line) appears shorter than 64 hex characters; if accurate, `makepkg` would reject it at the integrity check rather than bypassing anything. Neither observation indicates malicious behavior.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Standard font PKGBUILD: pinned checksums, HTTPS upstream, normal install steps, no malice.</summary>
</security_assessment>
